standard_prerequisites.name: For a finite type morphism over a quasi-compact base a sufficiently high power of an ample sheaf is very ample, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the proof replace the given sheaf by a power that is very ample.

standard_prerequisites.name: The pushforward of the structure-like sheaf along a quasi-projective morphism is quasi-coherent, and quasi-projective morphisms are quasi-compact and separated, cited from the schemes chapter and the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the pushforward of the sheaf a quasi-coherent module and gives the quasi-compactness used later.

standard_prerequisites.name: A quasi-coherent module is the filtered colimit of its finite type submodules, cited from the properties chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the finite type modules over which the construction of the morphism is made.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of very ample sheaves on an affine chart by finitely many generating sections and the resulting immersion into a projective space, and permanence of immersions
standard_prerequisites.use: Give the local immersions and show that the globally constructed morphism is an immersion.

standard_prerequisites.name: The statement that an immersion which is quasi-compact factors through an open immersion into a closed subscheme of its target, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the intermediate scheme X' inside the projective bundle.

core_obligations: Normalize the sheaf: since the morphism is of finite type and the base is quasi-compact, replace the ample sheaf by a high enough power to make it very ample (proof lines 10724-10727).

Approximate the pushforward: the pushforward of the sheaf is quasi-coherent, hence the filtered colimit of finite type submodules, and one considers the induced maps from the pullbacks of those submodules into the sheaf (proof lines 10729-10741).

Make one of those maps surjective: cover the base by finitely many affine opens, on each choose finitely many generating sections defining a local immersion into a projective space, and choose a finite type submodule whose sections lift all of them; the corresponding map is then surjective over the whole base (proof lines 10742-10755).

Build the global morphism and check it is an immersion: the surjection defines a morphism into the projective bundle of that finite type module, which over each affine open factors through the local immersion, hence is an immersion by permanence (proof lines 10756-10767).

Conclude projectivity: the morphism is quasi-compact, so the quasi-compact immersion statement produces a closed subscheme of the projective bundle through which it factors as an open immersion, and that closed subscheme is projective over the base by definition (proof lines 10768-10774).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a very ample sheaf and write its pushforward as a filtered colimit of finite type modules (proof lines 10724-10741).

Choose one member of the colimit surjecting onto the sheaf using finitely many affine charts, obtain an immersion into a projective bundle, and factor it through a closed subscheme via the quasi-compact immersion statement to reach projectivity (proof lines 10742-10774).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a quasi-projective morphism with quasi-compact quasi-separated base factors as an open immersion followed by a projective morphism (statement lines 10717-10722). The counted proof is substantial: it first replaces the ample sheaf by a power that is very ample, writes the quasi-coherent pushforward as a filtered colimit of finite type modules, covers the base by finitely many affines, lifts finitely many generating sections of the sheaf on each chart to a single member of the colimit so that the induced map becomes surjective, builds the resulting morphism into the projective bundle of that module, checks it is an immersion by factoring it through the local immersions, and finally applies the quasi-compact immersion statement to obtain a closed subscheme of the projective bundle through which the morphism factors as an open immersion (proof lines 10724-10774). It is H2: the construction and all its verifications are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard very ampleness, colimit and immersion statements.
